32b99b8.summary: Closure callback run after the execute swarm animation finishes. It finishes resolving the action: reassembles minions, checks for a dead hero and ends the match (sets result, Elo/XP, saves, sends match-finished), or else clears the resolving flag and re-enables turn controls.
comments: Closure callback: runs when the action animation ends; 'outer' is the BattleManager that queued it.
Count queued actions; if this was not action type 7 and the queue is empty, tidy up unit positions.
If a side's minions are out of place on the board, queue a reassemble order for that side.
No automatic actions left: check whether a hero died. Skipped in tutorial and campaign matches.
Hero state 5 seems to mean dead. If neither hero is dead, jump to the normal resume path.
Someone's hero died: remember whether it was the player's, then build and log the 'DeadHeroAfterActionsEnd' text.
Already in the post-battle stage: normally log a warning and stop, unless a disconnect loss is pending.
Disconnect-loss flag set: record an Enemy win and run the basic end-of-battle sequence instead.
Normal ending: enter post-battle stage and stop the battle; tell the other client the match finished if networked.
Lock the UI into the finish-battle state and clear the 'during battle' flag.
If the player won, raise a signal zeroing the enemy hero's health bar.
Look up the current event; ranked events (leaderboard) supply an Elo rating, otherwise the player's stored Elo is used.
Decompiler expanded an interface-method lookup here; it just calls the event's Elo rating getter.
Work out the winner and create the ranked match result with Elo and XP.
Fill the result's skull milestones: own skulls, and the enemy's skulls based on the player hero's remaining health.
Store the result and winner, then record the match length in minutes from the start time.
On a player win, flag a win and notify live-ops for certain match types (0x14, 0xb4, 0xd2) that the opponent was human.
Save the winner, finish the battle and return; the rest of the callback is skipped.
Decompiler artifact: array-bounds failure path of the log string builder.
No hero died (or tutorial/campaign): broadcast the 'while in play' trigger check.
Action fully resolved: clear the resolving-action flag.
Enemy's turn: reactivate enemy minions and refresh the enemy hero's attack state.
Hero can attack only with no tutorial restriction, not stunned and not summon-sick; this sets shade and canAttack.
Ferocity or oath heroes get their shade recomputed and may switch attack type while summon-sick.
Show or hide the hero's attack button depending on whether it can attack now.
Player's turn (decompiler reuses the heroCard name for the BattleManager): relight playable cards, activate minions and hero.
Queue empty: start the GC pass, unpause the turn clock and rebuild the available actions list.
In a tutorial, check whether ending the turn is permitted.
If the only action left is ending the turn, show the 'no actions left' UI on the clock.
In scripted tutorials, if the player just acted manually, resume the scripted turn once the AI script stops waiting for them.
Reset the manual-action marker.
Shared null-reference throw target.

32b9a58.summary: Coroutine that plays back recorded replay actions one at a time for the current turn, waiting one second between steps. It runs each action, decrements the replay queue and restores time scale when finished.
comments: States 2 and 3 are wait steps; state 0 logs the start and falls into the main loop.
State 2: if no replay actions remain, stop; otherwise run the next one.
State 3: keep waiting while actions are queued or neither side may act; then reset time scale to 1 and end.
State 1: resume after the one-second wait; abort if the manager is gone.
If actions are still being processed or neither side may act yet, wait another second.
Restore normal time scale unless a flag asks to keep the current (replay fast-forward) speed.
Log the player and enemy replay indices and actions left.
Run the next logged action for whichever side's turn it is (player or enemy log).
Decrement the replay queue; if more remain, wait and continue in state 2.
Queue is empty: start the ReplayPlayAction coroutine if it is not active, else wait while speed is 15x.
Decompiler artifact: string array bounds failure path.

32b9e98.summary: Coroutine at battle start that deals each side its environmental cards: spawns the defensive card into hand, shows and applies the offensive card, and waits between steps. Which cards belong to which side depends on who goes first.
comments: State 1 (after reveal wait): show the offensive button for the hero's army and destroy the revealed card.
State 0: look up the defensive and offensive card ids from the match data, depending on who goes first.
If there is a defensive card id, find it in the full card collection and add it to the starting side's hand.
Defensive card id not in the collection: log an error.
No offensive card id: nothing to do, end.
Decide whether to show the offensive card (it is skipped if it is an empty one).
Reveal the offensive card on screen and wait two seconds.
State 2: reveal done; apply the offensive card's effect.
Apply the environmental effect; if it was shown, wait four seconds before finishing.
Offensive card could not be found: log an error.

32ba4f0.summary: Coroutine that counts down once per second while trying to reconnect to the battle server. It re-attempts every third second, updates the UI, and reports success or failure when the countdown ends.
comments: State 1: one second passed; decrement seconds left and retry the connection every third second.
Stop if the connection is no longer in the trying-to-reconnect state.
Arithmetic trick for 'secLeft divisible by 3'; then ask the network manager to retry.
State 0: seconds allowed = max(10, max reconnect time minus 3 per previous disconnect minus 3); count this disconnect.
Continue while fewer than 6 disconnects and time remains and still reconnecting: update status UI and wait one real second.
Countdown over or connection state changed: log the final connection status.
Still not reconnected: tell the UI reconnection failed.
Otherwise report successful reconnection.
Decompiler lost the tail here; it ends by throwing an exception that reports the final status, which looks unreachable in practice.

32bab50.summary: Coroutine for the standard end of a battle: after a short wait it logs the result, hides the cemetery and chat button, and kills the losing side's units with death delays. Forfeit and disconnect results skip ahead; a win-button result calls CompleteBattleFinished.
comments: State 0 waits one second; state 1 starts the actual end sequence.
Log the winner and battle result.
Hide the cemetery and chat button.
Remember whether the player lost, and whether it was a forfeit (no warlord death sound then).
Enemy did not win: destroy the enemy's units (player victory path).
Wait time = minion death time per unit plus the warlord duration, or 2 seconds without globals.
Continue to the player side: if the player lost, destroy the player's units the same way.
Later states, keyed on the battle result: forfeit goes on to destroy units.
Disconnect falls through to a half-second wait; win button starts CompleteBattleFinished.
Short half-second wait before the final state.

32bb110.summary: Coroutine that handles a choose-a-card effect: builds the pool, asks the player (via UI) or enemy (AI) to pick, waits for the selection and passes the chosen index to the callback.
comments: State 1: loop that waits while the UI is still in the card-choice state.
Keep waiting a frame while the player is choosing.
Choice made: convert the chosen card into its index in the pool.
State 0: build the full choice pool for this action.
Empty pool: call back with index 0 and stop.
Player's action: open the card choice UI; enemy's: the AI picks immediately.
Deliver the chosen index to the callback.

32bb2c4.summary: Coroutine that shows the 'targetting' tooltip above the acting card and highlights valid targets, waiting until the player picks a unit target, then hides the tooltip and pauses the clock.
comments: If the game is already back to normal, the target was chosen while the unit played: do nothing.
Start tracking the card, unpause the turn clock, and show tooltip text just above the card.
Highlight the potential targets for a card played from hand.
Keep waiting while still choosing a target.
Target chosen: stop tracking, hide the tooltip and pause the clock for animation.

32bb5f4.summary: Coroutine that closes the end-of-battle doors: hides the HUD, sets up the doors with the result, skull count and winner, disables touch input and waits before marking the match finished and waiting to leave.
comments: State 1 (after the door wait): mark the match as finished and waiting to leave.
State 0: stop tracking and enable the end-of-battle door object.
Hide the battle HUD with animation.
Gather match result data and skull count for the door display; SetupDoor returns the time to wait.
Disable touch input, then wait for the door animation.

32bb840.summary: Coroutine run when a battle ends: waits for the ranked match result to finish processing, then sets the post-battle UI state, leaves the battle room and shows the share button.
comments: State 2: processing finished; go to the post-battle UI and leave the room.
Keep the room alive if the enemy won by the player's forfeit; otherwise leave normally.
Leave the battle room on the network and show the share button if one exists.
State 1: after the wait, check whether the result is processed.
State 0: if the result status is 2, wait two real seconds first.
Wait until the result has finished processing, then pause a quarter second before state 2.

32bba98.summary: Coroutine that waits a clip's delay and then plays a body animation on the target unit. If the clip does not wait for completion, the finish callback is called immediately.
comments: State 0: store the onFinish callback and wait for the clip's delay.
State 1: find the target unit from the clip's target type.
Not waiting for completion: fire the finish callback now.
Waiting: pass a wrapper so the callback runs when the animation ends.
Play the body animation on the target unit.

32bbcd8.summary: Coroutine that waits an effect's VFX delay, resolves start and end transforms if not already given, and spawns the animation.
comments: State 0: wait the VFX delay if it is positive.
Resolve start and end transforms from the animation's position options when no start parent was given.
Create the VFX animation between the two points.

32bbecc.summary: Coroutine that kills a side's warlord and then each of its minions one by one after battle end, waiting between deaths, used by the end-of-battle sequence.
comments: State 0: kill the hero first, if its object still exists and is active.
Mark the hero destroyed and start its death animation, then wait the warlord death time.
Units missing: log an error.
State 1: kill the minions from the last to the first.
Walk the minion list backwards; for each active minion mark it destroyed and start its death.
Wait a fraction of a second between minion deaths.
All minions handled: wait the final delay.
States 2 and 3: after each death delay, continue the loop or end.

32bc488.summary: Coroutine that plays a campaign scripted turn: keeps asking the scripted AI manager to play the next action, waiting between actions, until none remain, then clears the scripted flag and calls onComplete.
comments: State 2: after the wait; keep going if more scripted actions remain.
More scripted actions: wait a second and resolve the next one.
No more actions: clear the scripted-actions flag and call onComplete.
State 1: play the next scripted action and wait the time the script asks for.
State 0: count the coroutine, log it, and bail out with a warning if there is no scripted data.
Flag that scripted actions are running, reset the action counter and go to the loop.
